subject: Finex - throughput & latency SLOs / post-call next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chang <emily.chang@finex.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Finex - throughput & latency SLOs / post-call next steps

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size a short POC: 

Recap (per call):
- Primary workload: real-time compliance assistant for trader chat logs and order annotations. Typical completion length ~120 tokens, max 512 tokens for expanded context.
- Streaming required: yes — partial outputs to the client UI within first RTT are important for UX.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end (Redwood + network) target <= 300ms for short completions (<=256 tokens).
- Throughput / concurrency: Finex expects ~20 RPS steady with peak burst windows up to ~200 RPS. Peak concurrent sessions estimated ~180–200.
- Average tokens/request (as discussed defensively): we used 150 tokens in our spreadsheet; please confirm.

Initial quantified sizing we discussed (please confirm):
- Steady-state: 20 requests/sec * 150 tokens = 3,000 tokens/sec
- Peak: 200 requests/sec * 150 tokens = 30,000 tokens/sec
- Expected concurrency: steady ~40 active concurrent model contexts (due to KV caching + short sessions), peak ~400 concurrent contexts during spikes
- Streaming concurrency: ~20 concurrent streaming sessions steady, up to ~200 at peak

Action items / next steps:
1) Emily / Tom: confirm the average tokens/request (120–180 range), ± which model variants you want to test (open model or Redwood-verified). Also please attach a small sample of representative prompts/payloads (we discussed a 1-week sample).
2) Marissa / Neha / Rafael (internal): we’ll size a dedicated POC config and share expected GPU footprint and cost estimate.
3) Emily: if procurement wants to start early, please share procurement timeline and any contract constraints (DPA, IP, retention).
4) Emily: upload the API spec and a sample payload file — we can ingest payloads to run a quick tokens-per-request distribution.

Attachments: finex-workload-snapshot.csv (sample rows from our call notes)

I’ll follow up with a draft mutual action plan and a quick sizing note later next week.

Thanks,
Rafael

Subject: Re: Finex - throughput & latency SLOs / post-call next steps

Thanks Rafael — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Average tokens/request: after sampling our logs we see median ~120 tokens, mean ~150, 95th ~420 (when expanded context is passed). For initial POC please assume avg 130 tokens and plan headroom for 95th.
2) Concurrency: our internal EDF indicates steady concurrency ~25 active sessions, peak concurrent sessions during end-of-day processing windows ~180. We expect short spikes for certain market events.
3) Streaming: yes, streaming is required. Our UI expects first partial token within ~150ms of request start; overall 95th end-to-end completion target for short responses ~300ms as you noted.
4) QPS/Throughput: steady ~20 qps, peak bursts up to 200 qps sustained for 2–3 minute windows.
5) Security/compliance: we will need a SOC2 SAQ and an overview of data retention/audit logs for the POC. Procurement will also want an initial term sheet.

Attached: finex-api-specs.pdf and a small sample file finex-sample-payloads.json (snippet) — these contain anonymized payloads.

Next: please share your recommended POC sizing + estimated cost and any constraints for streaming on the chosen model. Procurement is looped in (procurement@finex.com) and may reach out separately.

Best,
Emily Chang

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Finex - throughput & latency SLOs / post-call next steps

Thanks for the quick data, Emily — super helpful. Based on your confirmation we’re proposing the following for an initial 4-week POC: 

POC Proposal (summary):
- Target profile: streaming-enabled model (Redwood-verified gpt-medium-like variant) with KV cache enabled for short sessions.
- Expected baseline sizing: 1x heavy GPU cluster that can sustain ~35k tokens/sec peak headroom (this maps to ~200 RPS @ 150 tokens with safe headroom for 95th percentile bursts).
- Concurrency config: session-based routing with 50 steady concurrent contexts and autoscaling to ~450 concurrent contexts during peak bursts.
- Latency expectation: we’ll aim to demonstrate 95th percentile end-to-end <300ms for <=256 token completions in our environment; streaming first-token latency typically <120ms on our test path.
- Metrics/telemetry we’ll deliver: per-request latency histogram, token/sec, active contexts, streaming chunk RTT, and failure/queue events.

Action items (mutual):
- Finex (Emily/Tom): confirm final sample payload set and provide a 1-week anonymized log extract (we received sample but need more representative distribution) and confirm which data center region you prefer (us-east).
- Finex: share procurement timeline and any contract constraints; procurement@finex.com is on copy.
- Redwood (Marissa/Neha/Rafael): deliver a short sizing note (GPU type and expected hourly cost), a template SOC2 SAQ response, and a proposed mutual action plan with milestones (POC start, evaluation checkpoints, procurement/commercial review).

I’ve attached a small preliminary sizing CSV (finex-workload-snapshot.csv) that shows the simple tokens/sec calcs we discussed.

If that looks good I’ll push a HubSpot deal update and send the mutual action plan + DocuSign term sheet for procurement to review.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Internal note before we send the MAP / pricing:

Summary of internal sizing and ask: 
- Use a single dedicated cluster configuration with the following recommended starting point: 4x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent in our offering) with automatic burst capacity to add 2 additional nodes for sustained peak windows. This aligns with the ~35k tokens/sec target and allows for streaming headroom and retries.
- Configure prefix/KV caching aggressively for trader-session contexts to reduce average active contexts by ~2.5x on short sessions.
- Suggested POC duration: 4 weeks with evaluation checkpoints at week 1 and week 3 (latency, cost, correctness).
- Commercial ask: draft 90-day trial pricing with consumption cap aligned to expected tokens/sec during POC plus an overage rate. Rafael — can you confirm whether we want to offer any initial credits if procurement pushes on price?

Next steps for Rafael: finalize the MAP, include SOC2 template and the DocuSign link to the POC term sheet. I’ll sync with infra to validate GPU sizing and confirm cost estimates.

-Marissa
